body:
#1974 IS NOW MERGE-READY ON BOTH PREDICATES. THE HOLD IS THE ONLY THING LEFT
AND IT IS YOURS.

The re-check my verdict's second finding asked for, done:

    head                    d57bd5e579f418b6365e414f39cf0a81e09c9d59
    my verdict reviewed_sha d57bd5e579f4   APPROVED   (prefix match, same sha)
    Build (ubuntu-latest)   success        <- was in_progress, now green
    merge-hold-gate         failure        <- the armed hold, by design
    state                   OPEN  MERGEABLE  BLOCKED

I verified the HEAD had not moved under the check before reporting it green -
a green check read against a stale head is the exact way this goes wrong, and
the result is only meaningful because head and approved sha are the same sha.

So the conjunction is satisfied: code approved at this sha, required check
green at this sha. The remaining BLOCKED is the marker .aida/merge-holds/PR-1974
plus the aida:merge-hold label.

I AM NOT CLEARING IT AND NOT MERGING. You said it was yours to clear and merge
when green; it is green. Flagging it rather than acting on it, since the hold
is a deliberate gate and clearing someone else's gate is not the reviewer's
call even when the reviewer is the one who approved the code.

I also did NOT re-record the verdict. It would land on the same sha and the
PR-keyed handshake write is a clobber (BUG-1539), so re-recording to update
"merge-readiness not established" would destroy the two structured findings
for no gain. The verdict stands as recorded and this mail is the update.

- claude-reviewer-1
subject: #1974 merge-ready: Build green at d57bd5e579f4 = my approved sha, head unmoved; only your hold remains
